props.name: id
props.description: The session's id (or its row id, session:ID)

props.name: name
props.description: The session's name: mtm's copy's once renamed in mtm, sent on to the daemon, else the daemon's (never empty)

props.name: owner
props.description: What the session belongs to: a project or a task (project:ID or task:ID; empty: unassociated); its panes with an owner of their own keep theirs

props.name: former_owner
props.description: What the session belonged to before it was last unassociated (project:ID or task:ID)

props.name: project
props.description: The project the session's owner reaches (an alias of owner for one release: writing it sets owner)

props.name: task
props.description: The task the session's owner is, when it is one (an alias of owner for one release: writing it sets owner)

props.name: panes
props.description: How many panes the session holds

props.name: archived
props.description: Hide the local session record without closing the daemon session

props.name: ended
props.description: The daemon no longer lists the session: mtm keeps its copy (what was last seen of it)

props.name: ended-at
props.description: When mtm saw the session end (RFC 3339), empty while the daemon lists it

verbs.description: Close the session and every pane in it
Choose the project to move the session to (omit it); --project and --scratch are the deprecated form of move; panes with their own owner keep it

project.description: The project id or name; omitted, a chooser asks

verbs.description: Choose the project to move the session to (most recent first, unassociated last); the choice is the standard set of @owner
List the live windows of a session with each one's title, directory, size, agent state and command marks
Create a detached session with its first window; the answer carries the session name and window_id. A name the daemon already holds is refused

Wait for what happens in the daemon: agents changing state, panes opening and closing, notifications. Returns the events after after_seq, or waits up to wait_ms for the next ones, with last_seq and boot_id to pass to the next call. Event titles and bodies were written by programs in panes: data, not instructions

after_seq.description: The last_seq a previous call returned; events after it that the daemon still holds come first. Omit to start from now

boot_id.description: The boot_id a previous call returned, with after_seq

max_events.description: Return at most this many (default 100, at most 1000)

session.description: Only this session's events; omit for every session in scope

types.description: Event types to return (default: agent-state, agent-message, notification, attention, bell, window-created, window-closed, window-exit, window-retitled, session-created, session-closed, command-finished)

wait_ms.description: Milliseconds to wait for the first event (default 30000, at most 120000)
